get.description: Returns a single bill, i.e. an accounts payable (AP) record of money the organization owes a vendor, by its ID. The bill is in the same shape as an item of the list endpoint (getBooksBills): its `id`, `referenceNumber` (the bill number), `vendor` (with `id` and `name`; omitted when the bill has no recorded vendor), `effectiveDate` (bill date), `dueDate`, `status`, `displayStatus`, `grossAmount` (total of all lines), `amountRemaining` (still owed after applied payments), `lines` (each with its ledger ID, i.e. general ledger (GL) account, description, and amount), and `paymentApplications` (each a line entry ID and the amount applied). `status` is the stored lifecycle status (`draft`, `open`, `processing`, `paid`, `cancelled`); `displayStatus` is what users see, which also distinguishes `overdue` and `partiallyPaid`. A vendor's `id` is a Books counterparty ID, not a recipient ID. Amounts are in dollars. The ID must be a bill: an unknown id or an invoice returns 404, and an id from another Books instance returns 403. To discover bill IDs, use the list endpoint (getBooksBills).

schema.description: The ID of the bill to retrieve, as returned by getBooksBills or createBooksBill.
The Books instance to act on. Must be the token organization's own instance, which it defaults to.

patch.description: Edits an existing bill, i.e. an accounts payable record, and returns the updated bill. Every field is optional; an omitted field is left unchanged. Editable fields: `vendor` (an existing Books counterparty id — unlike create, a recipient alias is not accepted on edit), `referenceNumber`, `effectiveDate` and `dueDate` (both YYYY-MM-DD), `notes`, and `lineChanges`. `lineChanges` has three optional lists: `create` (new lines, each with a `ledgerId`, `description`, and dollar `amount`), `update` (existing lines by `id`, each field optional), and `delete` (existing line `id`s). As with create, a line amount may be negative, zero-amount lines are ignored, and the lines must total more than zero. The response is the updated bill, in the same shape the create and retrieve endpoints return. Limits: a cancelled bill cannot be edited. A paid bill accepts only changes to existing lines' `ledgerId`. A bill matched to a transaction that is not yet fully paid (partially paid) can still be edited, but its total and each line's amount cannot drop below what has already been paid on it, and a line with payments cannot be deleted (Teal enforces these). A paid or matched bill with accrual schedules cannot be edited. A bill created from Bill Pay may only have its line categories (`ledgerId`) changed; any other change is rejected. Request errors are returned as an HTTP error status and change nothing: the token lacks the scope to update accrual sources, a line ledger is outside the Books instance or read-only, or the vendor counterparty does not belong to this organization. The `id` must be a bill: editing an invoice through this endpoint returns 404, as does an unknown id. To make retries safe, send an `Idempotency-Key` header: a `lineChanges.create` is not naturally idempotent, so without a key a retry after a timeout can append duplicate lines; a replay with the same key and body returns the original result instead (a reused key with a different body is rejected with 422).

get.description: Returns one page of a Books instance's bills: accounts payable (AP), money the organization owes vendors. A vendor's `id` is a Books counterparty ID, which is not a recipient ID. Amounts are in dollars. Each response is one page of at most `limit` items (default 100, at most 1000). To see every match, pass `nextPageToken` back as pageToken with the same other parameters, and repeat until a response has no `nextPageToken`. To read specific bills by ID, pass their IDs as `ids`. To discover ledger IDs, use getBooksLedgers.

post.description: Creates a single bill, i.e. an accounts payable record of money the organization owes a vendor, which books the matching journal entries. The bill needs a `vendor` — a tagged object `{"tag": ..., "contents": ...}` naming either an existing Books counterparty (`{"tag": "counterpartyId", "contents": ...}`) or a banking recipient (`{"tag": "recipientId", "contents": ...}`, resolved to its linked counterparty) — an `effectiveDate` (the bill date) and `dueDate` (both YYYY-MM-DD), and at least one line in `lines`. Each line needs a `ledgerId` (the expense ledger to book it against, from getBooksLedgers), a `description`, and an `amount` in dollars; a line amount may be negative (e.g. a discount); zero-amount lines are ignored, at least one line must be non-zero, and the lines must total more than zero. `referenceNumber` (e.g. the vendor's bill number) and `notes` are optional. The response is the created bill: its `id`, `vendor` (always a counterparty id), `status`, amounts (`grossAmount`, `amountPaid`, `amountOutstanding`), `lines`, and generated `journalEntryIds`. To make retries safe, send an `Idempotency-Key` header: a replay with the same key and body returns the original bill rather than creating a duplicate (a reused key with a different body is rejected). Without one, a retry after a timeout can create a second bill. If a request fails with a server error (HTTP 5xx), the bill may already have been created, so a retry with the same key returns 409 (the original attempt is treated as still in progress); check whether the bill exists rather than retrying with a new key, which could create a duplicate. Request errors are returned as an HTTP error status and create nothing: the token lacks the scope to create accrual sources, a line ledger is outside the Books instance or read-only, the vendor counterparty or recipient does not belong to this organization, or the lines fail Teal's validation.

get.description: Lists every close recorded for the Books instance, sorted by `closeDate`, latest first. The first item is the current close date; the list is empty when the books have never been closed. Each close has its `closeId` and its `closeDate` (`YYYY-MM-DD`), the last day the books are closed through. Closes are soft: they are recorded but not enforced, so journal entries dated on or before a close can still be created and edited.

schema.description: The Books instance to act on. Must be the token organization's own instance, which it defaults to.

post.description: Closes the books through `closeDate` (`YYYY-MM-DD`), which must be today or earlier (UTC) and after the latest close date, or, when the books have never been closed, on or after the day the books' entries start; any other date is a 400 that names the rule. A `closeDate` equal to the latest close date returns 200 and changes nothing, so retrying the same request is safe. A 503 means Books couldn't close the books or couldn't confirm the close; retry the same request. The close is soft: it sets the close date reports use and doesn't lock journal entries dated on or before it. To list existing closes and the latest close date, use getBooksCloses.

get.description: Lists the Books instances, i.e. organizations' books (their general ledger: chart of accounts, journal entries, and reports), that this token can act on. Call this first, then pass an instance's `booksId` as the `booksId` argument of the other Books operations, such as the list ledgers endpoint (getBooksLedgers). A token can only act on its own organization's Books instance, so this lists at most that one instance; where `booksId` is optional, the token may omit it. Each instance has its `booksId`; the `organizationId`, `companyName`, and `callsign` of the organization it belongs to; and its `relationship` to the token's organization, which is `self`. Lists exactly the instances the other Books operations would let this token act on, given the scopes those operations need: the token's user must be an active member of the instance's organization with permission to manage Books, code transactions, and manage accounting integrations, and with access to all of its accounts, and the organization must have access to Books. An empty list means there is no instance this token can act on. Instances are sorted by `companyName`, ignoring case, and returned a page at a time: when the response has a `nextPageToken`, pass it as `pageToken` to get the next page.

get.description: Returns the connection health of every integration a Books instance syncs data from: external bank and credit card accounts (Plaid), Stripe and PayPal accounts, and Gusto payroll. Use it to judge whether the books are complete enough to trust before reporting on them. Each entry in `integrations` is one existing connection, with `integrationId` (unique only within its `provider`), `name`, `provider` (`plaid`, `stripe`, `payPal`, or `gusto`), `connectionStatus`, `lastSyncedAt` when known, `sourceAccountId` when it feeds a source account, and `requiredAction`. `connectionStatus` is `autoSynced` (healthy), `setupInProgress` (first sync running), `setupPending` (waiting for the user to finish setup), `syncPaused` (paused by the user), `connectionLost` (broken; no new data arrives), or `inactive` (disabled; do not treat it as connected). `requiredAction` names what the user must do: `reconnectInMercury`, `completeSetupInMercury`, `resumeSyncInMercury`, or `none`. All fixes must be done by the user in the Mercury app; the API cannot reconnect, resume, or finish setting up an integration. `lastSyncedAt` means different things per provider: for Stripe, PayPal, and Gusto it is the last successful pull from the vendor into Mercury; for Plaid it is the last successful push from Mercury into Books. No staleness flag is returned; judge staleness from it. A provider the organization never connected has no entry, and neither has a removed Plaid connection, so a missing bank entry doesn't tell never-connected from removed. Mercury accounts and manual accounts are never included; to list every transaction feed, including those, use `getBooksSourceAccounts`. `failedChecks` lists the areas whose health could not be checked (`externalBanks`, `commerce`, `payroll`). For a listed area, health is unknown, not broken: don't treat its missing providers as never connected, and don't tell the user to reconnect them. When `failedChecks` is empty, a missing provider was never connected.

get.description: Returns a single invoice, i.e. an accounts receivable (AR) record of money a customer owes the organization, by its ID. The invoice is in the same shape as an item of the list endpoint (getBooksInvoices): its `id`, `referenceNumber` (the invoice number), `customer` (the customer billed, with its `id` and `name`; omitted when the invoice has no recorded customer), `effectiveDate` (invoice date), `dueDate`, `status`, `displayStatus`, `grossAmount` (total of all lines), `amountRemaining` (still owed after applied payments), `lines` (each with its ledger ID, i.e. general ledger (GL) account, description, and amount), `notes` (omitted when none), and `paymentApplications` (each a line entry ID, such as a bank transaction's line, and the amount of it applied). `status` is the stored lifecycle status (`draft`, `open`, `processing`, `paid`, `cancelled`); `displayStatus` is what users see, which also distinguishes `overdue` (open and past due) and `partiallyPaid` (open with some payment applied). A customer's `id` is a Mercury Invoicing customer ID, as used by the Mercury Invoicing customers API (`/ar/customers`); a deleted customer still appears with its name. Amounts are in dollars. The ID must be an invoice: an unknown id or a bill returns 404, and an id from another Books instance returns 403. Every field is optional; an omitted field is left unchanged. Editable fields: `referenceNumber` (the invoice number), `customer` (a Mercury Invoicing customer ID of this organization, from the Mercury Invoicing customers API, `/ar/customers`), `effectiveDate` (invoice date) and `dueDate` (both YYYY-MM-DD), `notes`, and `lineChanges`. `lineChanges` has three optional lists: `create` (new lines, each with a `ledgerId`, i.e. a general ledger (GL) account such as a revenue ledger, a `description`, and a dollar `amount`), `update` (existing lines by `id`, each other field optional), and `delete` (existing line `id`s). On an invoice synced with Mercury Invoicing, `customer` may be sent only as the invoice's current customer, which is accepted; a different customer is rejected with an error on `customer`. Request errors are returned as an HTTP error status and change nothing: the token lacks the scope to update accrual sources, a line ledger is outside the Books instance or read-only, or the customer does not belong to this organization. The `id` must be an invoice: a bill ID returns 404 (use updateBooksBill to edit bills), as does an unknown id. To remove a ledger's parent, list `parentId` in `clearFields` (and don't also set `parentId`). Each `ledgerId` may appear at most once.

**Chart-of-accounts rules.** Teal validates each update: `subType` must belong to `type` (see the `type` and `subType` fields of a ledger, as returned by getBooksLedgers); a child ledger has the same type and sub-type as its parent, so a sub-ledger can't be retyped in place; a parent can't be the ledger itself or one of its descendants; names and sort codes must be unique; required ledgers allow changes only to `name`, `sortCode`, and `parentId`; expense and revenue ledgers can't be cash-flow ledgers, so a cash-flow ledger can't be retyped to either; and ledgers linked to a financial account may refuse some changes.

A ledger that fails does not fail the request or the other ledgers, so the status is 200 whatever the item outcomes. The response's `failedCount` is 0 exactly when every item succeeded, and `succeededCount` plus `failedCount` equals the number of results; when `failedCount` is above 0, check each result's `error`. Error codes include `invalidLedger`, `missingParameters`, `duplicateName`, `duplicateSortCode`, `invalidLedgerType`, `invalidLedgerParent`, `invalidLedgerReportCashFlow`, `modifyingRequiredLedger`, and `unknownError`; treat any code not listed here as `unknownError`.

delete.description:
Deletes up to 100 ledgers, i.e. general ledger (GL) accounts, from the organization's chart of accounts, by ledger ID. To find ledger IDs, use getBooksLedgers. Ledgers are deleted one at a time in request order, so list each child ledger before its parent: a parent listed before its child still has that child when it is reached and is not deleted. A repeated ID is processed once, at its first position. This operation never deletes journal entries.

**Per-item results.** The response has one result per distinct requested ID, in request order: its `ledgerId` and `deleted: true`, or `deleted: false` with an `error` that has a stable `code` and a `message` saying how to fix it. A ledger that fails does not fail the request or the other ledgers, so the status is 200 whatever the item outcomes. The response's `failedCount` is 0 exactly when every item succeeded, and `succeededCount` plus `failedCount` equals the number of results; when `failedCount` is above 0, check each result's `error`.

**Per-item error codes (`error.code`) and how to fix them:**

- `deletingLedgerWithActivity`: the ledger has activity, such as line entries. Move or delete its journal entries first; this operation won't delete them.
- `deletingParentLedger`: the ledger still has child ledgers. Delete its children first, or list them before the parent in the same request.
- `deletingLinkedLedger`: the ledger is linked to a bank or other source account. Unlink the account first.
- `deletingRequiredLedger`: the chart of accounts requires this ledger. It cannot be deleted.
- `integrationMapped`: an accounting, invoicing, commerce, or Plaid integration is mapped to the ledger. Remove the mapping first.
- `unknownError`: the ledger could not be deleted for another reason. Read `message`; retry, or treat any code not listed here the same way.

The run has the fields of an item of getBooksPayrollRuns (`id`, `runType`, `payPeriodStart`, `payPeriodEnd`, `postingDate`, `totalPayroll`, `employerCost`, `matchingStatus`), plus `amountPaid` (already matched to payments), `amountOutstanding` (what a payment can still be matched to: `totalPayroll` net of payments and adjustments), `initialAccrualJournalEntryId` (the journal entry that recorded the run, omitted when there is none), `relatedJournalEntryIds` (every journal entry touching the run: the initial accrual and the entries of payments matched to it; read one with retrieveBooksJournalEntry), and `lines`. Each line has its `sourceLineId`, `description`, `amount`, `amountPaid`, `amountOutstanding` (`amount` less `amountPaid`), `matchingStatus`, and `matchable`; only matchable lines can be matched to a payment. Before matching a payment to the run, read `amountOutstanding` on the run and on its lines. Amounts are in dollars; a line's `amount` and `amountOutstanding` are negative for an offset or reversal. An unknown ID returns 404, and an ID from another Books instance returns 403. To discover payroll run IDs, use getBooksPayrollRuns.

post.description: Records that a transaction's line entry, a bank withdrawal, paid one or more payroll runs, i.e. matches the payment to them. Payroll runs come from the organization's connected payroll provider; each is one pay period's payroll, which Books records as an accrual awaiting payment. Use the transaction's own `lineEntryId` from getBooksTransactions or getBooksTransaction, and payroll run IDs from getBooksPayrollRuns. Before matching, read each run's `amountOutstanding` with getBooksPayrollRun. Each item of `applications` gives a `payrollRunId` and the positive `amount` of the payment applied to that run, as a JSON number of dollars with at most two decimal places. A run may take a partial amount, less than its `amountOutstanding`, but never more. An application may carry `adjustments`, which write off part of that run's remaining balance; a run's `amount` plus its adjustments can't exceed its `amountOutstanding`. The request's own `adjustments` are closing adjustments on the line entry, for any part of the payment no run accounts for, such as a bank fee. Each adjustment is a `ledgerId` (an editable ledger, i.e. general ledger (GL) account, of the instance, from getBooksLedgers) and a positive `amount` in dollars with at most two decimal places; each adjustments list may have at most 100 items, and all adjustments together may name at most 100 different ledgers. List every run the payment covers in one request, from 1 to 100 runs, each at most once: a line entry is matched at most once, and the applied amounts plus the closing adjustments must add up to the transaction's amount (a run's own adjustments don't count toward it). The transaction's other lines are replaced by lines for the matched runs and adjustments, so an existing split is removed and the transaction's category can change. 400, and nothing changes, when an ID isn't a payroll run of the Books instance (a bill or invoice ID included) or the request is malformed. 403, and nothing changes, when an adjustment ledger is read-only or in another Books instance; a ledger Books can't otherwise post to is refused with 400. 409, and nothing changes, when the line entry is already matched differently. A 503 response means Books couldn't match the line entry or confirm the match right now; retry the same request. Retrying the same request is always safe: a retried request whose match already landed succeeds without matching again. Returns 204 with no body on success; to see the result, read the runs back with getBooksPayrollRun, whose `amountPaid` and `matchingStatus` reflect the match. To undo a payroll match, unmatch the line entry with deleteBooksPaymentApplications.

Ledgers, i.e. general ledger (GL) accounts, that the rule already applied to transactions stay in place; deleting a rule does not un-categorize anything. Only rules that getBooksCategorizationRules returns can be deleted; any other ID, including the organization's other automation rules that Books doesn't show, is a 404. get.description: Returns the categorization rules of a Books instance that Books can represent (see the end of this description for which are omitted), highest priority first: the rules that automatically categorize imported transactions to ledgers, i.e. general ledger (GL) accounts. When several rules match a transaction, the first one in this order applies. Rules are returned a page at a time, 50 by default and up to 100 with `limit`: when the response has a `nextPageToken`, pass it as `pageToken` to get the next page. A page token is a position in the priority order, so a rule added, deleted, or reordered between page requests can shift which rules the remaining pages hold: a rule moved across the position can be listed twice or not at all. Rules can also occasionally be renumbered while you page; if that happens, a page may skip or repeat rules, so restart from the first page if you need an exact snapshot. Each rule has: `id`; `conditions`, the conditions a transaction must match, at least one, all of which must match (logical AND; there is no OR, so an "any of" rule is written as separate rules); `outputs`, what the rule does to a matching transaction; `status`: `active` (it categorizes matching transactions), `inactive` (disabled), or `invalid` (no longer valid, so it categorizes nothing); `glCodeName`, the display name of the GL account it categorizes to; and `lastApplied`, the last time it matched a transaction. Each condition is an object whose `tag` says what it tests and whose `contents` holds its fields: `amount` (`operator`, one of `lessThan`, `lessThanOrEqualTo`, `greaterThan`, `greaterThanOrEqualTo`, or `equalTo`, and `amount`, a threshold in dollars), `description` (`contains`: the raw bank description contains this text, ignoring case), `counterparty` (`name`: the counterparty name is exactly this), `debitCard` (`debitCardId`), `creditCard` (`creditCardId`), `user` (`userId`: the team member who made the transaction), or `customCategory` (`customCategoryId`: the transaction's Mercury custom category). Amounts are signed: money in (credits) is positive and money out (debits) is negative, and the threshold is compared against the signed amount as is, so `lessThan` -50 matches outflows of more than $50. Each output has a `tag` and `contents` the same way; the only one today is `setLedger`, whose `ledgerId` is the ledger matching transactions are categorized to (look it up with getBooksLedgers). Rules Books can't represent are omitted: rules with a condition or output outside this vocabulary, such as accounting-integration rules that set a Mercury custom category, and rules whose GL account no longer maps to a Books ledger. So this list can be shorter than the organization's full rule list, and an omitted rule can still take precedence over a listed one.

The rule only applies to transactions categorized from now on; it does not re-categorize existing transactions. The body has `conditions` (1 to 10, all of which must match; logical AND, there is no OR) and `outputs` (at most one of each kind, so today exactly one `setLedger`), in the same shape getBooksCategorizationRules returns, so a listed rule's `conditions` and `outputs` can be sent back as is. Each condition has a `tag` and `contents`: `amount` (`operator`, one of `lessThan`, `lessThanOrEqualTo`, `greaterThan`, `greaterThanOrEqualTo`, or `equalTo`, and `amount`, a signed threshold in dollars: money in is positive and money out negative), `description` (`contains`), `counterparty` (`name`), `debitCard` (`debitCardId`), `creditCard` (`creditCardId`), `user` (`userId`), or `customCategory` (`customCategoryId`); every card, user, and custom category must belong to the organization. The only output is `setLedger` (`ledgerId`), a ledger the caller may edit (not read-only) in the Books instance; to find ledger IDs, use getBooksLedgers. There is no priority field: the new rule is placed among the existing rules by how specific its conditions are, and the first matching rule applies. Returns the created `rule`, in the shape getBooksCategorizationRules returns. A rule that doesn't validate, a ledger without a GL account, or conditions the organization already has a rule for are a 400 and create nothing; to see existing rules, use getBooksCategorizationRules.

post.description: Sets the categorization of one or more posted bank transactions, all or nothing. Each item names a transaction by its `journalEntryId` and gives its new categorization as `splits`: one split per category, each with the `ledgerId` of the ledger, i.e. general ledger (GL) account, to categorize to (such as an expense or revenue account) and the signed `amount` of the transaction that goes to it, as a JSON number of dollars with at most two decimal places. One split categorizes the whole transaction to one ledger; several split it across ledgers. Splits use the same sign convention as the transaction's `amount` from `GET /books/transactions` (getBooksTransactions), must be nonzero, and must add up to exactly that `amount`; a split with the opposite sign, such as a refund netted against a purchase, posts on the other side. A split may set the line's `description` and `tagIds`; omit them to keep those of the line it replaces. The splits replace every current categorization line of the transaction; its bank line on the source account's ledger is never changed. The last write wins: if the transaction was recategorized after you read it, this request overwrites that change. A split's ledger must belong to the Books instance and be editable, and must not be an uncategorized income or expense ledger or a source account's ledger. Only journal entries of bank transactions can be categorized, and a transaction matched to a transfer between accounts must be unmatched first. Send from 1 to 100 items, each transaction at most once; across all items, the splits may name at most 100 different ledgers. If a `journalEntryId`, split `ledgerId`, or tag ID doesn't exist, the whole request fails with 404, and if one belongs to another Books instance, or a split's ledger is read-only (linked to a Mercury account), with 403; no transaction is changed. A few problems fail the whole request with 422 and a `message` saying why, such as two tags from the same tag group on one split; no transaction is changed. Every item is checked before anything changes: if any item is invalid, no transaction is changed, and the 400 response's `errors.errorCode` is `invalidCategorizationItems` with `errors.itemErrors` listing every problem, each with its 0-based `itemIndex` into `items`, a `code`, and a `message`. The codes are `duplicateJournalEntry`, `journalEntryNotFound` (the journal entry was deleted while the request ran), `notTransactionSourced`, `transferMatched`, `splitsDoNotSumToTransactionAmount`, `invalidSplitAmount`, `ledgerNotFound` (the ledger was deleted while the request ran), `ledgerNotEditable`, `ineligibleLedger` (a split's ledger can't take a transaction's categorization, such as the opening balances ledger or an accounts receivable or payable ledger), `uncategorizedLedger`, `sourceAccountLedger`, and `unknownError` (any other problem, described by its `message`); more may be added, so treat an unrecognized code as `unknownError` and show its `message`. On success, every transaction has the requested categorization, and the response lists each one's new `categorizationLines`, in request order. A 500 response doesn't mean nothing changed: Books may have applied the items, so read the transactions again before retrying. To find transactions and their current categorization, use `GET /books/transactions` (getBooksTransactions); to find ledger IDs, use `GET /books/ledgers` (getBooksLedgers).

BooksAPILedgerBalance.description:
One ledger's balances over the requested date range.

 Amounts are signed by the ledger's natural side: a positive amount is an
 increase on the side named by `debitCredit` (a debit ledger such as an asset
 grows with debits, a credit ledger such as a liability grows with credits),
 and a negative amount is a decrease. Balances are not flipped to a common
 debit-positive convention.

 Balances cover only the ledger's own line entries; they do not roll up the
 balances of its child ledgers. To get a parent's total, request its children
 as well and sum them, using `parentId` from the list ledgers endpoint.
 Opening-balance entries count. The Retained Earnings and Current Year
 Earnings system ledgers also include the calculated earnings, so their
 balances match the balance sheet. A ledger with no activity reports zeros.

allOf.description: The balance at the end of `endDate`.
Whether the ledger has a natural debit or credit balance, which is the side that positive amounts increase.

The ledger's more specific accounting classification.

ReimbursementPaymentStatus.description:
Payout state, separate from review.

- `pending`: no payout in progress. The reimbursement isn't approved yet, or it's approved and waiting for a payout batch. A canceled payout, or one Mercury retries automatically, also returns to `pending`.
- `initiated`: the payout is in progress.
- `paid`: the payout completed.
- `failed`: the payout failed. Mercury retries in a later batch once the submitter fixes their payout account, unless they've left the organization.
- `paidOutsideMercury`: an approver recorded that the submitter was paid outside Mercury, so Mercury won't pay it. Its review status is `approved`.

ReimbursementReviewStatus.description:
Review state, separate from payment.

- `submitted`: waiting for review.
- `updatesRequested`: a reviewer asked the submitter for changes.
- `approved`: a reviewer approved it. `paymentStatus` shows the payout.
- `denied`: a reviewer denied it.
- `canceled`: the submitter canceled it.
